subject: Architecture
title: The Charles Bridge: Prague's Medieval Marvel
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Charles Bridge: Prague's Medieval Marvel.

hook.text: Legend says eggs were mixed into the mortar of Prague's Charles Bridge. Scientists found it's actually true.

buildup.text: Construction began in 1357 under Charles IV. Sixteen stone arches span 1,693 feet across the Vltava River.

discovery.text: Thirty Baroque statues line the bridge — saints, angels, and a golden cross mark this open-air gallery.

twist.text: Protein from eggs in the mortar actually improves durability — the bridge has survived 660 years of floods.

climax.text: Today 30,000 tourists cross it daily. Charles IV laid the first stone at 5:31 AM — an astrologically chosen time.

punchline.text: Eggs, astrology, and Gothic stonework. Prague's oldest bridge still stands.

quiz.question: What unusual ingredient was mixed into the Charles Bridge's mortar?
options: Eggs, which improved the mortar's durability
